column2: Israel's evil and the Lord's handing over to Midian for seven years remain; the duration is not harmonized with other oppression cycles.
Midian's prevailing hand leads Israel to make enclosures in mountains, caves and strongholds; the hand image and three locations remain.
A singular Israelite sower is opposed by Midian, Amalek and the eastern peoples, with repeated came up and singular against him retained.
Camping shifts to against them; ruined produce reaches Gaza and no livelihood remains, including flock, calf and donkey. Calf preserves the selected moschos here.
Invaders, livestock, carried tents, locust-like multitude and innumerable camels all remain, with the purpose of ruining Israel's land.
Israel's great poverty from Midian precedes the cry to the Lord; the causal relation remains.
The repeated cry because of Midian introduces the next unit's response, without deleting the repeated information.
The Lord sends a man who is a prophet, whose speech explicitly identifies the Lord as Egypt's deliverer and recalls the house of slavery.
Rescue from Egypt and all oppressors, expulsion and the gift of their land remain as separate divine actions.
The quoted prohibition concerns fear of the Amorites' gods in their land, followed by failure to obey My voice; no service prohibition is substituted for fear.
The messenger sits at Joash's oak in Ephrathah; Joash is father of Abiezri in the selected wording, and Gideon threshes wheat in a winepress to escape Midian.
column3: The relation of father of Abiezri to the subsequent his son and the Ephrathah place identification remain open; no Ophrah/Abiezrite reconstruction is made.

column2: The messenger announces the Lord's presence and mighty strength; the inherited vocative mighty man of strength interprets the nominative phrase as address.
column3: The strength phrase's attachment and messenger identity remain provisional, not grounds for expanding divine titles.

column2: Gideon's please/my lord, inclusive us, all evils, all wonders and the fathers' Egypt question remain before the present rejection complaint; ordinary address to the messenger is preserved.
The selected messenger of the Lord looks and commissions Gideon, promises salvation and says Behold, I have sent you; the speaker is not silently replaced with the Lord.
Gideon questions his means of saving, names his thousand in Manasseh and his small status in his father's house; the selected social-number term remains.
column3: Thousand's clan/military sense and the comparative tapeinotera rendered lowliest need specialist review; no clan replacement is imposed.

column2: The messenger says the Lord shall accompany Gideon, who will strike Midian as one man; third-person Lord and singular collective enemy image remain.
The favor condition leads to a request for a sign that you are speaking with me; ordinary you leaves the messenger identity open, and the future is rendered as a request in context.
The stay-until-return request includes bringing a sacrifice and setting it before the visitor; I am here and I will sit remain in the answer.
column3: Here supplies the locative sense of the elliptical I am reply; it is not treated as a separate divine-name declaration.

column2: The goat, oiphi of unleavened flour, meat on the basket, broth in the pot, oak location and bowing remain; the selected on relation is preserved.
column3: Oiphi remains an identified source measure without a modern conversion; bowing's devotional force and messenger identity are not resolved here.

column2: Meat and plural unleavened loaves are set by the rock, with broth poured out; the location is not silently changed to on the rock.
The messenger's staff touches the food, fire comes from the rock and consumes both meat and unleavened cakes, and the messenger leaves Gideon's sight; all repeated food terms remain.
Recognition leads to repeated Ah and Lord, Lord, and the face-to-face statement; the repeated address is not reduced to one title.
The Lord's peace and prohibition of fear about death remain in the inherited linked form.
column3: The relationship of mē phobou to mē apothanēs needs syntactic review against an independent you shall not die rendering; no certainty about the clause division is claimed.

column2: The altar is named Peace of the Lord and the selected Ephrathah/father of Ezri wording remains through the present-day notice.
column3: The final being-there clause's subject and the relation of Ezri to Abiezri in 6:11 remain unresolved; no name normalization is applied.

column2: The selected father's fattened seven-year bull and destruction of Baal's altar and grove remain; no second bull is imported.
column3: Bull reflects the explicit seven-year animal context, unlike the younger-animal working rendering of moschos at 6:4; this is not a global lexical substitution.

column2: The altar goes to the Lord who appeared, on Mount Maoz's summit in battle array; the whole burnt offering uses the grove wood you will cut down, retaining the final future.
column3: Mount Maoz and in battle array remain textual/lexical questions; no familiar stronghold or orderly-arrangement paraphrase is imposed.

column2: Thirteen men accompany Gideon, whose fear of household and townsmen leads to night action; the selected thirteen is not replaced with ten.
column3: Servants is the inherited rendering of douloi in the household setting; the underlying servile status is not thereby ruled out and needs glossary-level review.

column2: The morning discovery retains Behold, demolished altar, cut grove and the offered fattened bull on the built altar; newly makes the narrative sequence explicit rather than identifying a separate adjective.
The neighbors' question, examination, search and naming of Gideon son of Joash remain; the doubled this thing is retained.
The demand to bring out the son to die is justified by both altar demolition and grove cutting; neither action is omitted.

Restore Or before the second question for explicit ē. Retain now, the death-by-morning statement, conditional god claim and the difficult he/him/one references without resolving them into a familiar defense speech.
column3: Who disputes, who dies and who avenges whom remain disputed; the final anonymous one renders the implicit subject without naming Gideon or Baal.

column2: The selected neuter it is named Tribunal of Baal because of the altar demolition; this is not replaced with a direct renaming of Gideon as Jerubbaal.
column3: The namer and named object remain implicit/uncertain; the next chapter's Jerubbaal identification does not resolve this unit by itself.

column2: All Midian, Amalek and eastern peoples gather, cross and camp in Jezreel valley; the three movement stages remain.
The Spirit of God clothes Gideon, who sounds a horn, and Abiezer cries behind him; the clothing image is not replaced with generic empowerment.
Messengers go through all Manasseh, which also cries behind Gideon, then through Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali, who come to meet him; both missions remain.
Gideon's explicit prayer to God retains Thou art saving and Thou hast spoken, with his hand as the instrument and Israel as recipient.
Behold, wool fleece, threshing floor, dew on the fleece alone and dryness on all ground form the condition for knowing the promised salvation; divine Thou repeats consistently.
The event occurs, Gideon rises next day and squeezes the fleece, and its dew fills a basin; the selected flowing verb remains.
Thy wrath, two once-more requests and the reversed fleece/ground condition remain; no explicit Thee is added as testing's object where the Greek leaves it implicit.
God performs the reversed sign that night: fleece alone dry and all ground dewy; both contrastive locations remain.
Jerubbaal is explicitly identified with Gideon, camping at Aroed while Midian and Amalek lie north by Abor in the valley; selected names and both enemy groups remain.
Too many people would enable Israel's boast against God; My own hand expresses the contrastive human boast, and the negative purpose remains explicit.
The Lord directly commands the fearful return notice; departure from Mount Gilead, twenty-two thousand returning and ten thousand remaining are retained.
The repeated too-many assessment leads to water testing and two opposite go-with-you decisions; all repeated instructions remain.
Tongue-lapping like a dog and kneeling to drink receive separate setting-aside commands; neither group is omitted or prematurely identified as chosen.
The tongue-lappers total three hundred; all others kneel to drink. No hand-to-mouth description absent from the selected line is supplied.
Save you all marks plural hymas, contrasting with Gideon's singular your hand. The dismissal of the other people is distributive, each to his place.
Provisions and horn trumpets are taken by plural they; singular he dismisses Israel's men while retaining the three hundred, with Midian below in the valley.
column3: The opening takers are implicit, contextually the retained force; the pronoun is not replaced with an invented explicit group.

column2: The night command includes rise, descend quickly from here and the completed gift into Gideon's hand; quickly and the locative here remain.
Fear conditions the alternative descent with Purah, Gideon's servant; the human companion is not replaced by a messenger.
column3: Paidarion can denote a young attendant; servant is retained without asserting either age or legal status as fully settled.

column2: Hearing speech will strengthen Gideon's hands before descent; the actual descent with Purah reaches a section of the fifty, preserving the selected unusual number.
column3: Section of the fifty is an unresolved camp-organization expression; no armed-men or outpost reconstruction is inserted.

column2: The three enemy groups fill the valley like locusts, and camels are innumerable like seashore sand; both multitude images remain.

Three idou markers frame entry, the dream introduction and the rolling barley cake. Restore the third as behold before the cake, while the first two remain look. The tent is struck, overturned and falls.
The neighbor identifies the dream exclusively with Gideon's sword and credits the Lord with handing over Midian and the whole camp; nothing but represents the selected restrictive construction.
Hearing both dream account and interpretation leads to worship of the Lord, return and the plural command to rise because the camp is given into their hands.
Three hundred divide into three companies, with horn trumpets, empty water jars and torches inside; no later weapon is added to the initial equipment list.
Watching Gideon, imitation, Behold his entry into the camp's midst and repeated imitation remain; the midst is not changed to an edge.
The coordinated trumpet signal ends with For the Lord and for Gideon; sword is not added here from the later cry at 7:20.
Gideon and one hundred enter at the middle watch; restore But for plēn before the emphatic singular he roused the guards. Horns and jar-dashing remain subsequent plural actions.
column3: The guards' rousing and the implicit subject remain difficult; the selected action is not replaced by setting a fresh watch.

column2: Three companies blow and break jars, hold torches left and horns right, and cry A sword for the Lord and Gideon; the sides and fuller cry remain.
Each attacker stands separately around the camp; the whole camp runs, alarms and flees, preserving the contrast in movement.
The three hundred horns are grammatical subjects of sounding, and the Lord turns swords against neighbors; Beth-shittah, gathered together, Abel-meholah's edge and Tabbath remain.
column3: Gathered together is retained as the selected participle, not replaced with a reconstructed place name; the flight route remains provisional.

column2: Israel's men cry from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh and pursue Midian; no additional tribe is inserted.
Gideon's message commands descent and seizure of water to Beth-barah and Jordan; Ephraim's response repeats both water and boundaries, with beforehand for the prior-seizure verb.
Oreb and Zeeb are captured and killed at selected Sourin and Jakephzeeb, and their heads are brought from beyond Jordan; no translated rock/winepress names replace the selected forms.
column3: Greek has singular head before both names; English plural heads distributes the body part across two named persons rather than positing one shared head.
